newsitem.title: USA: ACXIOM sues Axiom alleging trademark infringement.
newsitem.headline: ACXIOM sues Axiom alleging trademark infringement.

text.p: ACXIOM Corp has filed a federal lawsuit seeking to block the former Securicor Telesciences Inc from using its newly adopted name of Axiom Inc.

In papers filed Friday in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, ACXIOM sought an emergency restraining order against Axiom's use of the name it adopted in May to replace its former trademarks, "Sterling" and "Manifest."

Both companies sell computer software to the telecommunications industry to collect and manage large databases of consumer information. ACXIOM alleges that "confusion...within the investment community" will result from the similarity of names and their identical pronunciation, and the overlap of products and stock symbols.

ACXIOM, of Conway, Arkansas, has been using its trademark since 1988. Axiom, of Moorestown, New Jersey, completed an initial public offering (IPO) on July 11 of 2.6 million shares of common stock at $12 a share. The company is controlled by Securicor Group plc SCCO.L which owns more than 50 percent of the stock, Axiom spokesman Mark Kadish told Reuters.
In addition to seeking a restraining order, ACXIOM has sked the court for unspecified damages, tripled because of the alleged "willfulness of Axiom's infringement."
Kadish said "We are aware of the lawsuit. We had addressed this in our (IPO) prospectus and we will actively pursue it. At this time we feel the claim does not have merit."
